key_insight: Error-conditioned neural solvers teach a neural model to recognize its own mistakes and use that signal to improve solution quality, rather than relying only on one-shot prediction. This aims to combine the speed of neural surrogates with a more reliable correction mechanism for PDE solving.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between fast neural surrogate solvers and physically accurate PDE solutions. Standard surrogates can violate constraints and fail out of distribution, while classical residual-correction methods are often too slow, unstable, or costly.
method: Condition the solver on an error/residual signal so it can learn when and how to self-correct.
Use the model’s predicted error to guide refinement toward lower PDE residuals and better constraint satisfaction.
Replace or reduce reliance on iterative classical optimization steps with a learned correction strategy.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could make neural PDE solvers more trustworthy in scientific and engineering settings where correctness matters. It offers a path to faster inference with improved physical fidelity and better robustness beyond the training data.
